summary: hex-encode-utils postinstall fetches encrypted payload from Cloudflare Workers and executes on the installer
details: package.json declares a postinstall hook that runs scripts/compat.js. On install, the script performs anti-analysis gating (skips when CI/container environment variables such as GITHUB_ACTIONS, DOCKER_CONTAINER, or KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST are set, and requires Desktop/Documents/Downloads directories to exist) and then fetches an AES-256-GCM encrypted blob from two hardcoded Cloudflare Workers hosts (steel-mere-4155.ricardorichp.workers.dev and cold-peak-7969.0x0gnx0.workers.dev) at path /e, decrypts it locally, writes the plaintext to ~/.cache/hex-encode-utils/modules/runtime.py, and spawns a detached Python process to execute the resulting file. In parallel, the script POSTs host identifiers (os.hostname, os.userInfo().username, os.platform, os.arch, Node version, package version) to /r on the same hosts, formatted as a Telegram-style chat notification with chat_id 6087129674. TLS certificate verification is disabled (rejectUnauthorized:false) on both requests. A comment self-labels the code as a 'Standard telemetry pattern' while the actual behavior is an encrypted install-time dropper with sandbox evasion.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
